text: Mulching, compost, and garden plants all play a vital role in maintaining the health and productivity of your garden. Mulch, often made of organic materials like wood chips, straw, or grass clippings, helps suppress weed growth, conserves moisture, and enriches the soil by adding nutrients as it breaks down. Compost, on the other hand, is the organic refuse from home composting or green waste recycling, offering a rich soil amendment that improves texture, drainage, and nutrient content. Gardening plants, whether annuals, perennials, or vegetables, bring biodiversity and beauty to your garden while providing sustenance for you and your ecosystem. By integrating these methods, gardeners can create a sustainable, thriving garden environment that is enriched with organic matter, supports a diverse range of plant and animal life, and enhances overall soil health.
